revision_reason: Addresses plan reviewer feedback: (1) FAIL_PIPELINE two-strike confirmation, (2) exception isolation at integration points, (3) HEALTH_CHECK_MODE operational kill-switch, plus minor observations on docs, circuit breaker thread safety, 2-PR decision justification, and test coverage.
title: Holistic pipeline failure detection: two-tier health check framework
summary: Revised architecture for a unified health check framework in the orchestrator. Key changes from v1: (1) HealthCheckRunner implements a two-strike confirmation mechanism for FAIL_PIPELINE actions — first occurrence is recorded but not enforced, only on repeated FAIL_PIPELINE from the same check on the next trigger is the action applied (critical false-positive protection per RISK-4/REC-2). (2) Runner catches exceptions from individual checks and returns DEGRADED/CONTINUE; all integration sites wrap run_checks() in try/except (REC-3). (3) HEALTH_CHECK_MODE environment variable (enforce/observe/disabled) controls runtime behavior without code changes (REC-4). (4) PhaseOutputPresenceCheck checks local branch head before remote. (5) Per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances avoid thread-safety issues (RISK-8). (6) Explicit exception isolation acceptance criteria on Phase 7 integration tasks. (7) Phase 8 includes exception isolation tests and RUNTIME_TICK performance test.

problem_statement.description: Pipeline failure detection is a collection of ad-hoc mechanisms built reactively for specific failure modes. startup_reconciliation.py handles crash recovery at startup, container_monitor.py detects container exits at runtime, signals.py records agent self-reported errors, and multi_agent.py has a blunt max_waves=5 iteration cap. None share a common abstraction, none produce structured verdicts, and none can detect semantic failures — cases where infrastructure is healthy but agents failed to accomplish meaningful work.
problem_statement.motivating_incident: Issue-835: reviewer containers exited cleanly (exit code 0), all structural checks passed, but reviewers had nothing to review because coders' work never reached the remote. Current mechanisms cannot detect this class of failure.
goals: Define a shared HealthCheck interface with structured HealthResult verdicts (HEALTHY / DEGRADED / FAILED) and suggested actions (CONTINUE / FAIL_PIPELINE / ALERT / RETRY)
Migrate startup reconciliation (#839) and container monitor (#848) to the new interface without changing observable behavior
Add Tier 1 programmatic checks: phase output presence (commits on remote), state consistency (orchestrator vs Docker), repeated failure patterns
Add Tier 2 agent inspector: LLM-based semantic evaluation of agent work quality
Wire trigger points into lifecycle: STARTUP, RUNTIME_TICK, WAVE_COMPLETE, PHASE_COMPLETE, ON_DEMAND
Surface health check results via the existing EventBus/SSE system for observability
Persist health check results in pipeline state for debugging (capped rolling window)
Implement two-strike confirmation for FAIL_PIPELINE to prevent false positive pipeline termination
Provide HEALTH_CHECK_MODE kill-switch for safe production rollout (enforce/observe/disabled)

startup_reconciliation.mechanism: reconcile_stale_containers(store, docker_client) runs once at startup from cli.py:cmd_serve(). Compares persisted RUNNING pipeline containers against live Docker set. Missing containers → agent marked FAILED → pipeline marked FAILED with error message 'Container not found at orchestrator startup'. No version check on save (startup-only, no concurrent writers). Returns int count of recovered pipelines.
startup_reconciliation.interface_gap: No structured verdict — returns int. No reason/action tuple. No event emission. Direct state mutation inline.

container_monitor.mechanism: ContainerMonitor class with background thread polling Docker every 10s (configurable check_interval). _check_container() detects state transitions via cached _container_states dict, emits ContainerEvent (STARTED/STOPPED/FAILED/REMOVED). create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() subscribes to FAILED events and calls _reconcile_container_state() which scans all RUNNING pipelines for the failed container, marks containers/agents/pipelines FAILED with optimistic locking (expected_version).
container_monitor.interface_gap: Uses its own ContainerEvent type (not shared HealthResult). State mutation is inline in the handler via _reconcile_container_state(), not mediated through a runner. Periodic orphan cleanup every 60 iterations.

signal_handlers.mechanism: Agents self-report via POST /pipelines/{id}/signal. handle_error_signal records failure in contract via dispatcher. handle_complete_signal records success and checks wave/phase completion.
signal_handlers.interface_gap: Reactive (agent-initiated only). No proactive detection capability. Trusts agent self-reporting.

iteration_caps.mechanism: execute_all_waves(on_wave_complete, agent_prompts, max_waves=5). on_wave_complete callback parameter exists but is NEVER passed in the single call site at pipelines.py:3260 — called as execute_all_waves(agent_prompts=agent_prompts_by_role) without the callback. When max_waves exceeded, logs warning and breaks. No structured verdict, no pipeline status update.
iteration_caps.interface_gap: Silent stop. Pipeline not marked FAILED. No structured reason provided. on_wave_complete hook exists but is unused — clean extension point.

event_system.mechanism: EventBus with typed EventType StrEnum. EventType.HEALTH_CHECK = 'system.health_check' already exists. Pub/sub with wildcard subscriptions, async delivery via worker thread, event history (max 100). Singleton via get_event_bus(). Convenience emit_event() function.
event_system.readiness: EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists. No new event types needed.

resilience_patterns.mechanism: agent_recovery.py: AgentRetryManager with RetryPolicy (IMMEDIATE/BACKOFF/ESCALATE/NO_RETRY), AgentRetryConfig (max_retries, retry_delay), RetryDecision. AgentCircuitBreaker with CircuitBreakerConfig (failure_threshold, reset_timeout) — NOT thread-safe (no locking, plain instance attributes). orchestrator/resilience.py: separate thread-safe CircuitBreaker class (uses threading.Lock) with global instances for container_spawn and gateway_api.
resilience_patterns.thread_safety_note: AgentCircuitBreaker is NOT thread-safe and is currently NOT used in production code. The orchestrator's own CircuitBreaker in resilience.py IS thread-safe. The HealthCheckRunner must use per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances accessed only under per-pipeline lock to avoid concurrent state mutation.

state_persistence.mechanism: Git-backed pipeline state on orphan branch egg/pipeline-state. StateStore with per-pipeline locking via get_pipeline_state_lock() (threading.RLock + fcntl.flock). Optimistic versioning via save_pipeline(pipeline, expected_version=N) → VersionConflictError on mismatch. Pipeline.version incremented on each save.
state_persistence.relevance: Health check state mutations must use per-pipeline locking and optimistic versioning to avoid races with concurrent signal handlers and the container monitor thread.

singleton_pattern.mechanism: Module-level _variable with get_variable() lazy-init getter function. Used consistently across EventBus, ContainerSpawner, StatusReporter. HealthCheckRunner should follow the same pattern.
singleton_pattern.relevance: HealthCheckRunner singleton should use this pattern: _runner + get_health_check_runner() in orchestrator/health/runner.py.

env_var_pattern.mechanism: os.environ.get(name, default) for configuration. Boolean flags use .lower() == 'true'. No explicit feature flag mechanism exists — HEALTH_CHECK_MODE will follow this pattern.
env_var_pattern.relevance: HEALTH_CHECK_MODE should use os.environ.get('HEALTH_CHECK_MODE', 'enforce').lower() with values: enforce, observe, disabled.

existing_http_health.mechanism: Flask blueprint with GET /api/v1/health (returns status, service, timestamp, component health), GET /api/v1/ready (returns {ready: true}), GET /api/v1/live (returns {alive: true}). Basic service health — no pipeline-level health checking.
existing_http_health.relevance: The on-demand pipeline health check endpoint (POST /api/v1/pipelines/<id>/health-check) should be added to the pipelines blueprint (routes/pipelines.py) since it operates on a specific pipeline, not the general health blueprint.

pipeline_models.key_models: Pipeline (id, status, current_phase, phases, config, version), PhaseExecution (phase, status, containers, agents, review_cycles, artifacts, error), AgentExecution (role, status, container_id, commit, outputs, error, retry_count), ContainerInfo (container_id, status, exit_code, agent_role), PipelineConfig (max_review_cycles, max_parallel_agents, etc.)
pipeline_models.relevance: HealthCheckResult model will be added here. PhaseExecution.health_checks field will store recent results.

key_files.role: Crash recovery at startup — detects missing containers
key_files.changes_needed: Wrap reconcile_stale_containers() logic in a StartupReconciliationCheck class implementing HealthCheck. Return HealthResult instead of int. Emit HEALTH_CHECK event. Keep original function as thin wrapper for backward compat during transition.

key_files.role: Runtime container failure detection via Docker polling
key_files.changes_needed: Extract _reconcile_container_state() evaluation logic into a ContainerLivenessCheck implementing HealthCheck. Update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to route through HealthCheckRunner. Monitor continues polling Docker and emitting ContainerEvents; the runner handles state mutation. Integration site MUST wrap run_checks() in try/except.
key_files.risk: Medium — concurrent thread with state access. Must preserve per-pipeline locking and optimistic versioning behavior.

key_files.role: Wave-based parallel agent execution with on_wave_complete callback
key_files.changes_needed: Wire on_wave_complete callback (line 545-546) to invoke HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=WAVE_COMPLETE). Pass wave results in PipelineHealthContext. The on_wave_complete callback is currently NEVER passed — this is a clean extension point. Callback MUST be wrapped in try/except — exceptions must not propagate to the execution thread. Replace silent max_waves stop with structured health check result.
key_files.risk: Medium — on_wave_complete runs from execution thread; checks must not block indefinitely. Exception isolation is critical.

key_files.role: Pipeline CRUD and _run_pipeline() orchestration loop (5543 lines)
key_files.changes_needed: Invoke HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=PHASE_COMPLETE) after phase completion in _run_pipeline(). Act on HealthResult.action. Changes must be surgical — single function calls at well-defined lifecycle points. ALL calls wrapped in try/except. Call site: _run_multi_agent_phase() at line 3260 should pass on_wave_complete callback to execute_all_waves().
key_files.risk: High — largest, most complex file. Changes must be purely additive (2-3 line insertions). No restructuring.

key_files.role: EventBus with pub/sub and EventType enum
key_files.changes_needed: None. EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists. Health check results emitted as events with structured data payload.
key_files.risk: None — no changes to EventBus itself.

key_files.changes_needed: Add HealthCheckResult model (check_name, tier, status, reason, action, timestamp, metadata). Add optional health_checks: list[HealthCheckResult] field to PhaseExecution (default_factory=list). Backward compatible — new field defaults to empty list.
key_files.risk: Low — additive model changes, optional field with default.

key_files.changes_needed: Add POST /api/v1/pipelines/{id}/health-check endpoint for on-demand health evaluation. Returns aggregated HealthResult for the pipeline. Document the endpoint.
key_files.risk: Low — additive endpoint on existing blueprint.

key_files.role: CLI entry point, calls cmd_serve() which starts startup reconciliation
key_files.changes_needed: Initialize HealthCheckRunner with all checks registered. Replace direct reconcile_stale_containers() call with runner.run_checks(trigger=STARTUP). Wrap in try/except for exception isolation.

key_files.role: Flask app creation and blueprint registration
key_files.changes_needed: No changes to api.py. HealthCheckRunner follows the codebase singleton pattern: module-level _runner + get_health_check_runner() in health/runner.py. Routes import the getter. This matches existing patterns (get_event_bus, get_container_spawner, get_status_reporter).

approaches.name: Unified HealthCheck interface with HealthCheckRunner
approaches.description: Define HealthCheck ABC, HealthResult, PipelineHealthContext, and Tier/Trigger enums in a new orchestrator/health/ package. Implement HealthCheckRunner that manages a registry of checks, runs them at trigger points, and applies results (emit events, optionally fail pipeline). Includes two-strike confirmation for FAIL_PIPELINE actions, exception isolation in runner and at integration sites, and HEALTH_CHECK_MODE kill-switch. Migrate startup reconciliation and container monitor. Add new Tier 1 checks and Tier 2 agent inspector. Wire triggers into lifecycle.
pros: Clean, composable abstraction — new checks are just new HealthCheck implementations
Unified HealthResult model standardizes all failure detection output with structured verdicts and actions
HealthCheckRunner centralizes result handling (event emission, pipeline state mutation, retry consultation)
Two-strike confirmation prevents false positive pipeline termination (RISK-4/REC-2)
HEALTH_CHECK_MODE enables safe production rollout starting in observe mode (REC-4)
Exception isolation at every layer prevents health checks from crashing pipeline execution (REC-3)
Trigger points declared on the check — easy to reason about which checks run when
Each check independently testable — inject mock PipelineHealthContext, assert HealthResult
EventType.HEALTH_CHECK already exists — observability via SSE for free
Lazy context assembly avoids expensive operations on fast triggers
Migration of existing mechanisms is mechanical — both follow gather→evaluate→mutate pattern
cons: New abstraction layer that all future failure detection must go through
Migration of existing mechanisms requires refactoring to separate evaluation from state mutation
PipelineHealthContext assembly adds complexity (lazy loading for git log, agent outputs)
Tier 2 agent inspector adds LLM API cost and latency at phase boundaries
New orchestrator/health/ package adds ~10 new files

approaches.name: Event-driven health evaluation (no new interface)
approaches.description: Extend the existing EventBus with new event types for health evaluation. Subscribe health evaluation functions as event handlers. Add new handlers for phase output presence and semantic checks alongside existing mechanisms. Keep startup reconciliation and container monitor as-is.
pros: No new abstraction — reuses existing EventBus pub/sub infrastructure
Minimal migration — existing mechanisms stay untouched
cons: No unified result model — each handler decides its own output format
Tier classification (programmatic vs agent) is implicit rather than explicit
Trigger management scattered across handler registrations instead of declared on checks
Harder to test individual checks in isolation (requires mocking EventBus)
Doesn't solve core problem — adds more ad-hoc handlers without shared structure
No centralized result application — each handler must implement its own state mutation

approaches.name: Tier 1 only (defer Tier 2 agent inspector to follow-up)
approaches.description: Implement approach A's HealthCheck interface and all Tier 1 programmatic checks. Defer Tier 2 (LLM-based agent inspector) to a follow-up issue. Establishes the interface cleanly for Tier 2 to slot into later.
pros: Reduced scope — delivers unified interface and highest-value checks without LLM complexity
Phase output presence check alone catches issue-835 scenario (no commits on remote → DEGRADED)
No API cost concerns for initial rollout
Establishes the interface cleanly; Tier 2 is purely additive later
cons: Defers semantic health evaluation that catches novel failure patterns
Some failures remain undetectable: reviewer reviewed nothing, coder changes don't address issue
Interface may need adjustment when Tier 2 is added if not designed with it in mind

recommended_approach.name: Unified HealthCheck interface with HealthCheckRunner
justification: The refine analysis recommended Option A and both refine reviewers (refine + agent-design) approved. The issue description provides a well-considered design for the full two-tier framework.

The interface pays for itself immediately. The HealthCheck/HealthResult/PipelineHealthContext trio provides a testable, composable abstraction that replaces ad-hoc state mutations with structured verdicts.

Migration is mechanical. Both startup_reconciliation.py and container_monitor.py already follow the 'gather context → evaluate condition → mutate state' pattern. Wrapping them in HealthCheck.check() with HealthResult return is straightforward.

Tier 2 should ship in the same change to establish the full framework. This validates the interface handles both tiers cleanly and avoids the risk of designing for Tier 1 only and needing to adjust when Tier 2 arrives. The Tier 2 inspector is scoped (Haiku model, structured evaluation, 30s timeout) and the LLM call pattern is well-understood.

The codebase has the infrastructure: EventType.HEALTH_CHECK exists, per-pipeline locking is battle-tested, resilience patterns are available, the singleton pattern (get_event_bus, get_container_spawner) is established.
Revision v2 addresses all reviewer concerns: two-strike confirmation (RISK-4/REC-2), exception isolation (REC-3), and HEALTH_CHECK_MODE kill-switch (REC-4) are now integral to the design.
recommended_approach.single_pr_justification: The risk analyst recommended considering a 2-PR split (REC-1: Tier 1 first, Tier 2 second). We ship as a single PR for these reasons: (1) The HealthCheck interface is designed for both tiers — shipping Tier 1 alone risks designing an interface that needs adjustment for Tier 2. (2) The HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=observe kill-switch provides the same safety as a staged rollout — deploy everything, start in observe mode, graduate to enforce. (3) Tier 2 adds exactly 2 files (llm_client.py, agent_inspector.py) with well-isolated scope — splitting adds coordination overhead for minimal risk reduction. (4) The integration wiring in Phase 7 is identical regardless of which checks are registered — the runner handles both tiers transparently. If review capacity is constrained, the PR can be reviewed in two passes: core+Tier1 first, then Tier2+wiring.

stages.name: Foundation: types, interface, runner, and model
stages.description: Define core abstractions in new orchestrator/health/ package and extend the pipeline model for result persistence.

phases.name: Health check types and interface
phases.description: Create the core type definitions and abstract base class for the health check framework.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/__init__.py — package init with public API exports

New orchestrator/health/types.py — HealthStatus enum (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/FAILED), Action enum (CONTINUE/FAIL_PIPELINE/ALERT/RETRY), Tier enum (PROGRAMMATIC/AGENT), Trigger enum (STARTUP/RUNTIME_TICK/WAVE_COMPLETE/PHASE_COMPLETE/ON_DEMAND), HealthResult dataclass (status, reason, action, check_name, tier, timestamp, metadata dict), HealthCheckMode enum (ENFORCE/OBSERVE/DISABLED) for the kill-switch

New orchestrator/health/context.py — PipelineHealthContext with lazy-loaded properties: pipeline (eager), phase_execution (eager), containers (eager), agents (eager), git_log (lazy — subprocess git log on worktree), git_diff (lazy — subprocess git diff), agent_output_files (lazy — filesystem glob), wave_results (optional, passed for WAVE_COMPLETE triggers), local_branch_head (lazy — git rev-parse for local branch head). Lazy fields use @cached_property. Context is created per-invocation — never cached or reused across triggers.

New orchestrator/health/base.py — abstract HealthCheck class with abstract properties tier -> Tier, triggers -> list[Trigger], name -> str, and abstract method check(context: PipelineHealthContext) -> HealthResult. Also: allow_immediate_fail -> bool property (default False) — when True, bypasses two-strike confirmation for checks where false positives are impossible (e.g., all containers verified gone from Docker).

phases.name: HealthCheckRunner with two-strike confirmation and kill-switch
phases.description: Implement the central runner that manages check registration, trigger filtering, execution, result application, two-strike FAIL_PIPELINE confirmation, and HEALTH_CHECK_MODE enforcement.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/runner.py — HealthCheckRunner class with: register(check: HealthCheck) adds to registry. run_checks(trigger: Trigger, context: PipelineHealthContext) -> list[HealthResult] filters checks by trigger, runs Tier 1 first, escalates to Tier 2 if Tier 1 returns DEGRADED or trigger is PHASE_COMPLETE/ON_DEMAND.

Two-strike confirmation for FAIL_PIPELINE: _pending_failures dict keyed by (pipeline_id, check_name). When a check returns FAIL_PIPELINE for the first time, store the result in _pending_failures and downgrade to ALERT (emit event, log warning, but do NOT fail the pipeline). If the same (pipeline_id, check_name) returns FAIL_PIPELINE on the next trigger, enforce the FAIL_PIPELINE action. Clear the pending entry when a check returns non-FAIL_PIPELINE. Exception: checks with allow_immediate_fail=True bypass two-strike (for cases where false positives are impossible, e.g., all containers verified absent from Docker).

HEALTH_CHECK_MODE support: read from os.environ.get('HEALTH_CHECK_MODE', 'enforce').lower(). 'enforce' mode applies FAIL_PIPELINE actions (with two-strike). 'observe' mode emits events and persists results but NEVER mutates pipeline state (all FAIL_PIPELINE/RETRY actions downgraded to ALERT). 'disabled' mode: run_checks() returns empty list immediately.

Exception isolation in runner: each individual check execution wrapped in try/except. If a check raises an exception, catch it, log the error, and return a synthetic HealthResult(status=DEGRADED, action=CONTINUE, reason='Check {name} raised {exception}') for that check. Never propagate check exceptions to the caller.

_apply_result(result, pipeline_id) emits HEALTH_CHECK event via emit_event(), persists result to PhaseExecution.health_checks (capped at 10). For FAIL_PIPELINE action in enforce mode: consults AgentRetryManager — if retries available trigger retry, else mark pipeline FAILED. Uses per-pipeline locking for state mutations. Configurable per-check timeout (default 5s for Tier 1, 30s for Tier 2).

Per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances: stored in runner._circuit_breakers dict keyed by pipeline_id. Created on first access. Accessed only under per-pipeline lock during _apply_result(), avoiding thread-safety issues (RISK-8). Cleaned up when pipeline completes/fails.
Singleton pattern: module-level _runner + get_health_check_runner() function, matching existing codebase patterns (get_event_bus, get_container_spawner).

phases.name: Pipeline state model extension
phases.description: Add HealthCheckResult model to pipeline state for persistence and observability.
key_changes: Modify orchestrator/models.py — add HealthCheckResult model (Pydantic BaseModel with: check_name: str, tier: str, status: str, reason: str, action: str, timestamp: datetime, metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}). Add health_checks: list[HealthCheckResult] = Field(default_factory=list) to PhaseExecution. Backward compatible — defaults to empty list.

stages.name: Migrate existing mechanisms
stages.description: Wrap startup reconciliation and container monitor detection logic in HealthCheck implementations. Preserve exact existing behavior.

phases.name: Migrate startup reconciliation
phases.description: Extract startup reconciliation logic into a HealthCheck implementation.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/__init__.py — package init

New orchestrator/health/checks/startup.py — StartupReconciliationCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[STARTUP], name='startup_reconciliation', allow_immediate_fail=True (stale container at startup is definitively not a false positive — the container is verifiably absent from Docker). check(context) compares persisted RUNNING containers against live Docker set (via docker_client in context). Returns FAILED with action FAIL_PIPELINE if stale containers found (with list of affected pipeline/container IDs in reason), HEALTHY otherwise. Does NOT mutate state — runner handles that.
Modify orchestrator/startup_reconciliation.py — deprecate reconcile_stale_containers() but keep as thin wrapper calling StartupReconciliationCheck for backward compat if anything imports it directly

phases.name: Migrate container monitor detection
phases.description: Extract container failure reconciliation logic into a HealthCheck implementation.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/container_liveness.py — ContainerLivenessCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[RUNTIME_TICK], name='container_liveness', allow_immediate_fail=True (container verified absent from Docker is definitively not a false positive). check(context) takes failed container info from context, scans RUNNING pipelines for the container, returns FAILED if pipeline has stale container(s), HEALTHY otherwise. Does NOT mutate state.

Modify orchestrator/container_monitor.py — update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to create handler that invokes HealthCheckRunner.run_checks(trigger=RUNTIME_TICK) with context containing the failed container info, instead of calling _reconcile_container_state() directly. Keep _reconcile_container_state() as deprecated backward-compat wrapper.

stages.name: New Tier 1 programmatic checks
stages.description: Add programmatic checks that detect failure modes not currently covered.

phases.name: Phase output presence check
phases.description: Check that phases produced expected artifacts. This is the check that would have caught issue-835.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/phase_output.py — PhaseOutputPresenceCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[PHASE_COMPLETE, WAVE_COMPLETE], name='phase_output_presence', allow_immediate_fail=False (uses two-strike confirmation — git push timing makes false positives possible).

check(context) evaluates based on current phase: implement → first checks context.local_branch_head for new commits on local branch since phase.work_started_at; if local has commits but remote doesn't (context.git_log shows no remote commits), return DEGRADED with reason 'Commits exist locally but not on remote — push may be in progress'; if neither local nor remote has commits, return DEGRADED with reason 'No commits found for implement phase'. plan → checks .egg-state/agent-outputs/ for architect/task_planner output files. refine → checks .egg-state/drafts/ for analysis document. Returns HEALTHY if present.

Key change from v1: checks LOCAL branch head first before remote, addressing the reviewer's concern that git push may still be in progress when the check runs. This prevents false positives from slow pushes.

phases.name: State consistency check
phases.description: Verify orchestrator state matches Docker reality during runtime.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/state_consistency.py — StateConsistencyCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[WAVE_COMPLETE, PHASE_COMPLETE], name='state_consistency', allow_immediate_fail=False (uses two-strike — transient Docker API errors could cause temporary state drift). check(context) verifies: containers marked RUNNING in pipeline state actually exist and are running in Docker (via docker_client), agents marked RUNNING have corresponding running containers, pipeline marked RUNNING has at least one active phase with active containers. Returns DEGRADED on drift (some containers gone), FAILED on critical inconsistency (all containers gone but pipeline RUNNING).

phases.name: Repeated failure pattern check
phases.description: Detect agents failing repeatedly with the same error, replacing the blunt max_waves cap.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/failure_patterns.py — RepeatedFailureCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=PROGRAMMATIC, triggers=[WAVE_COMPLETE], name='repeated_failure_pattern', allow_immediate_fail=False (uses two-strike — one bad wave shouldn't immediately kill the pipeline). check(context) examines agent execution history in current phase: if same role failed N times (configurable, default 3) with same/similar error, returns FAILED with action FAIL_PIPELINE and reason containing error pattern. Replaces the blunt max_waves silent stop with a smarter detection that explains why it's failing.

stages.name: Tier 2 agent inspector
stages.description: Implement LLM-based semantic health evaluation for detecting novel failure patterns.

phases.name: LLM client for orchestrator
phases.description: Thin wrapper for Anthropic API calls from the orchestrator context.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/llm_client.py — HealthInspectorClient class wrapping Anthropic API. Uses Haiku model for cost efficiency. Configurable model (default: claude-haiku). Structured output via JSON mode. Timeout: 30 seconds. Handles API errors gracefully (returns None on failure — inspector treats this as CONTINUE). Uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from environment. If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, log warning at startup and disable Tier 2 automatically. No connection reuse across invocations to prevent leaked connection state.

phases.name: Agent inspector implementation
phases.description: LLM-based check that evaluates whether agents produced meaningful work matching the phase goal.
key_changes: New orchestrator/health/checks/agent_inspector.py — AgentInspectorCheck implementing HealthCheck. tier=AGENT, triggers=[PHASE_COMPLETE, ON_DEMAND], name='agent_inspector', allow_immediate_fail=False (LLM verdict uses two-strike). check(context) assembles structured prompt with: (1) phase goal from contract, (2) agent output files content (context.agent_output_files), (3) git log/diff on worktree branch (context.git_log, context.git_diff), (4) agent execution results. Prompt asks LLM to evaluate work quality. Prompt includes explicit instruction to err on the side of DEGRADED over FAILED — FAILED requires clear evidence, not ambiguity. LLM returns structured JSON verdict: {status, reasoning, suggested_action}. Parses response into HealthResult. On LLM failure (timeout, API error, malformed response): returns DEGRADED with action CONTINUE.

stages.name: Lifecycle wiring and observability
stages.description: Wire health check trigger points into the orchestrator lifecycle. Every integration site wraps run_checks() in try/except for exception isolation.

phases.name: Wire trigger points into lifecycle
phases.description: Integrate HealthCheckRunner into the orchestrator's main execution paths with strict exception isolation at every integration site.
key_changes: Modify orchestrator/health/runner.py — add init_health_check_runner() function that creates the singleton, registers all checks (StartupReconciliation, ContainerLiveness, PhaseOutputPresence, StateConsistency, RepeatedFailure, AgentInspector), and returns the runner. Called from cli.py during startup.

Modify orchestrator/cli.py — call init_health_check_runner() at startup. Replace reconcile_stale_containers() with try/except wrapped runner.run_checks(trigger=STARTUP). Exception isolation: on any exception from run_checks(), log error and fall back to original reconcile_stale_containers() for safety.

Modify orchestrator/container_monitor.py — update create_pipeline_reconciliation_handler() to use runner. Handler wraps run_checks(trigger=RUNTIME_TICK) in try/except. On exception: log error and fall back to original _reconcile_container_state() for safety.

Modify orchestrator/multi_agent.py — pass on_wave_complete callback to execute_all_waves() in _run_multi_agent_phase(). The callback wraps runner.run_checks(trigger=WAVE_COMPLETE) in try/except. On exception: log error and continue — health check failure must NEVER block wave execution or crash the pipeline thread.

Modify orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py — invoke runner.run_checks(trigger=PHASE_COMPLETE) after phase completion in _run_pipeline(). Wrap in try/except. Act on results: FAIL_PIPELINE → mark pipeline failed, RETRY → trigger agent retry, ALERT → emit event only, CONTINUE → proceed. On exception: log error and continue — health check failure must NEVER block phase transition.

Modify orchestrator/routes/health.py — add POST /api/v1/pipelines/<pipeline_id>/health-check endpoint for on-demand evaluation. Returns aggregated health results as JSON. Document the endpoint with docstring describing request/response format.

stages.name: Testing
stages.description: Comprehensive test coverage for the health check framework including exception isolation and performance tests.

phases.name: Unit tests for types, context, runner, and individual checks
phases.description: Test each component independently with mock dependencies.
key_changes: New orchestrator/tests/test_health_types.py — test HealthResult creation, HealthStatus/Action/Tier/Trigger/HealthCheckMode enums
New orchestrator/tests/test_health_context.py — test PipelineHealthContext lazy loading, test that expensive fields aren't computed until accessed, test local_branch_head field

New orchestrator/tests/test_health_checks.py — test each HealthCheck implementation: StartupReconciliation (mock Docker, verify HEALTHY/FAILED, verify allow_immediate_fail=True), ContainerLiveness (mock pipeline state, verify detection, verify allow_immediate_fail=True), PhaseOutputPresence (mock git/filesystem, verify DEGRADED on missing outputs, verify local-before-remote check logic, verify allow_immediate_fail=False), StateConsistency (mock Docker vs state, verify drift detection), RepeatedFailure (mock execution history, verify pattern detection), AgentInspector (mock LLM client, verify structured verdict parsing and graceful failure handling)

New orchestrator/tests/test_health_runner.py — test HealthCheckRunner: trigger filtering (only matching checks run), Tier 1→Tier 2 escalation (DEGRADED triggers Tier 2), two-strike confirmation (first FAIL_PIPELINE is downgraded to ALERT, second FAIL_PIPELINE is enforced, allow_immediate_fail=True bypasses two-strike, non-FAIL result clears pending), HEALTH_CHECK_MODE behavior (enforce applies, observe emits only, disabled returns empty), exception isolation (check raising exception produces DEGRADED/CONTINUE result), result application (event emission, result persistence, cap at 10 results), per-pipeline circuit breaker instances, concurrent execution safety (per-pipeline locking)

phases.name: Integration tests, backward compatibility, exception isolation, and performance
phases.description: Test end-to-end lifecycle wiring, backward compatibility, exception isolation at integration sites, and RUNTIME_TICK performance.
key_changes: New orchestrator/tests/test_health_integration.py — test lifecycle wiring: startup trigger runs startup check, container failure triggers runtime check, wave complete triggers wave checks, phase complete triggers all checks including Tier 2, on-demand REST endpoint returns results. Mock Docker and LLM API throughout.

Exception isolation tests: verify health check exception does NOT crash _run_pipeline; verify health check exception does NOT crash container monitor handler; verify health check exception does NOT crash on_wave_complete callback; verify health check timeout does NOT block phase transition.
Backward compatibility tests: migrated startup reconciliation produces same state changes as original. Migrated container monitor produces same state changes as original.
Performance test: run 100 RUNTIME_TICK triggers with ContainerLivenessCheck, verify total time under 1 second and no git operations triggered (lazy context properties not accessed).
HEALTH_CHECK_MODE integration tests: verify observe mode emits events but does not fail pipelines; verify disabled mode skips all checks.

technical_decisions.decision: New orchestrator/health/ package rather than extending existing files
technical_decisions.rationale: The health check framework is a cohesive concern with its own types, interface, runner, and check implementations. orchestrator/health/ follows the same sub-package pattern as orchestrator/routes/. Avoids bloating existing files (especially the 5500-line routes/pipelines.py). Keeps checks independently testable and discoverable.
alternatives_considered: Add to container_monitor.py — rejected: mixes runtime monitoring with broader health check concern
Add to routes/pipelines.py — rejected: already 5500 lines, health checks aren't HTTP route logic
Flat files in orchestrator/ — rejected: 8+ new files would clutter the top-level directory

technical_decisions.rationale: Some fields are expensive: git log/diff requires subprocess calls to git, agent output files require filesystem reads. Runtime tick triggers happen every 10 seconds — eagerly computing all fields would add unnecessary overhead. Lazy properties (@cached_property) ensure a check that only needs container state never triggers git operations. Context objects are short-lived (per trigger invocation), so caching doesn't cause staleness.
alternatives_considered: Eager assembly with caching — rejected: cache invalidation is complex and most checks only need a subset
Pass raw pipeline object, let checks gather their own context — rejected: couples checks to orchestrator internals, prevents testing with mock context
Pre-filter context based on check requirements — rejected: over-engineering, lazy loading achieves same result naturally

technical_decisions.decision: Tier 2 agent inspector uses Haiku model
technical_decisions.rationale: The inspector's task is structured evaluation against a checklist. The input is well-defined and output is a structured JSON verdict. Haiku handles this well, is fast (~1-2s), and cheap. If Haiku proves insufficient, the model can be upgraded per-check without interface changes.
alternatives_considered: Use Sonnet/Opus — rejected: expensive and slow for a supervisory check at every phase boundary
No LLM (pattern matching only) — rejected: cannot detect novel failure modes, which is the core value of Tier 2
Configurable model per pipeline — considered but deferred: start with Haiku default, add config if needed

technical_decisions.decision: HealthCheckRunner applies results centrally — checks are pure evaluation functions
technical_decisions.rationale: Checks should be pure: context in, result out. The runner handles side effects (event emission, pipeline state mutation, retry consultation, two-strike confirmation, HEALTH_CHECK_MODE enforcement). This makes checks independently testable without requiring a real state store, prevents duplicate state mutations from concurrent checks, and centralizes the decision logic for FAIL_PIPELINE.
alternatives_considered: Checks mutate state directly (current container_monitor pattern) — rejected: scatters mutation logic, requires real state store for testing
Checks return results, caller applies at each trigger point — rejected: duplicates application logic across 5 trigger points

technical_decisions.decision: Health check results persisted in PhaseExecution.health_checks, capped at 10
technical_decisions.rationale: Results need persistence for debugging and observability but must not bloat pipeline state JSON. PhaseExecution is the natural home — health checks evaluate phase-level health. A rolling window of 10 results per phase provides enough history. At ~200 bytes per result, 10 results adds ~2KB per phase — negligible relative to the typical pipeline state.
alternatives_considered: Separate .egg-state/health/{pipeline-id}.json — rejected: adds another artifact with separate lifecycle management
Only emit events, don't persist — rejected: events are ephemeral (100 max in EventBus history), debugging needs historical results
Store in Pipeline.health_checks (top-level) — rejected: loses phase-level granularity

technical_decisions.decision: Tier 2 triggers: always at PHASE_COMPLETE, at WAVE_COMPLETE only on DEGRADED from Tier 1
technical_decisions.rationale: PHASE_COMPLETE is the natural checkpoint for semantic evaluation. Running Tier 2 at every WAVE_COMPLETE would be expensive. The DEGRADED trigger provides escalation: if Tier 1 detects structural anomalies, Tier 2 evaluates whether the anomaly is a real failure. ON_DEMAND via REST endpoint covers ad-hoc investigation.
alternatives_considered: Tier 2 at every trigger — rejected: prohibitive LLM cost
Tier 2 only on-demand — rejected: defeats automatic detection purpose
Tier 2 on a timer — rejected: not correlated with meaningful lifecycle events
Tier 2 only at PHASE_COMPLETE, never at WAVE_COMPLETE — considered but escalation from DEGRADED is valuable

technical_decisions.decision: FAIL_PIPELINE uses two-strike confirmation by default, with immediate-fail override for verified-true checks
technical_decisions.rationale: REVISION v2: Addresses RISK-4/REC-2. Automatic enforcement is powerful but a false positive destroys in-progress work. The two-strike rule provides a safety net: the first FAIL_PIPELINE result is recorded but downgraded to ALERT. If the same check returns FAIL_PIPELINE on the next trigger, the action is enforced. This handles transient conditions (slow git push, temporary Docker API error) without weakening detection for persistent failures. Checks where false positives are structurally impossible (e.g., startup reconciliation — container is verifiably absent from Docker) can set allow_immediate_fail=True to bypass two-strike. Additionally, the runner consults AgentRetryManager before failing: if retries available, trigger retry instead.
alternatives_considered: Advisory only (emit event, let caller decide) — rejected: existing code doesn't watch for health events, failure would be silently ignored
Always fail immediately (no delay) — rejected: false positives destroy in-progress work
Require Tier 1 AND Tier 2 confirmation — rejected: over-constrains Tier 1 checks that are deterministic and don't need LLM confirmation
Fixed time delay (e.g., 60 seconds) — rejected: trigger-based delay is more natural and adapts to pipeline pace

technical_decisions.decision: Inspector failures treated as DEGRADED/CONTINUE, not blocking
technical_decisions.rationale: The agent inspector is a safety net, not a gate. If the LLM API is down, returns malformed output, or times out, the pipeline should not be blocked. Returning DEGRADED with CONTINUE means the failure is logged and visible but doesn't prevent phase advancement.
alternatives_considered: Block on inspector failure — rejected: makes pipeline availability dependent on LLM API availability
Skip silently — rejected: losing visibility into inspector failures hinders debugging

technical_decisions.decision: HEALTH_CHECK_MODE environment variable (enforce/observe/disabled) as operational kill-switch
technical_decisions.rationale: REVISION v2: Addresses REC-4. Provides operational control without code changes. 'enforce' applies all FAIL_PIPELINE actions (with two-strike). 'observe' emits events and persists results but never mutates pipeline state — all FAIL_PIPELINE/RETRY actions downgraded to ALERT. 'disabled' skips all health checks. Default is 'enforce'. For initial production rollout, operators can start with 'observe' to build confidence, then graduate to 'enforce'. The env var follows the existing codebase pattern: os.environ.get('HEALTH_CHECK_MODE', 'enforce').lower().
alternatives_considered: Per-pipeline configuration flag — rejected: adds pipeline config complexity; env var is simpler for operational control
Feature flag service — rejected: no feature flag infrastructure exists in the orchestrator
Code-level boolean — rejected: requires redeploy to change; env var can be changed with container restart

technical_decisions.decision: Exception isolation at every layer — runner catches per-check exceptions, integration sites catch runner exceptions
technical_decisions.rationale: REVISION v2: Addresses REC-3. Health checks are a safety net. An unhandled exception in a health check must NEVER crash _run_pipeline(), the container monitor, or the HTTP server. Defense-in-depth: (1) The runner wraps each individual check execution in try/except and returns DEGRADED/CONTINUE for failed checks. (2) Every integration site (cli.py, container_monitor.py, multi_agent.py, pipelines.py) wraps its run_checks() call in try/except with logging and fallback behavior. This provides two layers of protection against unexpected exceptions.
alternatives_considered: Runner-level isolation only — rejected: defense-in-depth is better; a bug in the runner itself should also be caught
Integration-site isolation only — rejected: individual check exceptions should be isolated from each other within a single run_checks() call

technical_decisions.decision: Per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances in runner, not shared global
technical_decisions.rationale: REVISION v2: Addresses RISK-8. AgentCircuitBreaker in shared/egg_contracts/agent_recovery.py is NOT thread-safe (no locking). The orchestrator's own CircuitBreaker in resilience.py IS thread-safe but has different semantics (service-level, not agent-level). Solution: the runner stores per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances in _circuit_breakers[pipeline_id]. These are accessed only during _apply_result() under the per-pipeline lock (get_pipeline_state_lock), eliminating concurrent access to any single instance. Instances are cleaned up when a pipeline completes or fails.
alternatives_considered: Add threading.Lock to AgentCircuitBreaker — rejected: upstream change to shared library for a single consumer
Use orchestrator's thread-safe CircuitBreaker — rejected: different semantics (tracks service health, not per-pipeline agent health)
Skip circuit breaker consultation — rejected: valuable to bridge health checks and recovery system

technical_decisions.decision: Ship as single PR with HEALTH_CHECK_MODE as the rollout safety mechanism
technical_decisions.rationale: REVISION v2: Acknowledges REC-1 (2-PR split recommendation). We ship as a single PR because: (1) The HealthCheck interface is designed for both tiers — shipping Tier 1 alone risks needing interface adjustments for Tier 2. (2) HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=observe provides the same production safety as a staged PR rollout — deploy everything, start in observe mode, graduate to enforce. (3) Tier 2 adds exactly 2 files (llm_client.py, agent_inspector.py) — splitting adds coordination overhead for minimal risk reduction. (4) Integration wiring in Phase 7 is identical regardless of which checks are registered. If review capacity is a concern, the PR can be reviewed in two passes: core+Tier1 first, then Tier2.
alternatives_considered: 2-PR split (Tier 1 first, Tier 2 second) — considered per REC-1; rejected for reasons above, but valid if team prefers it

risks.description: routes/pipelines.py is 5543 lines and the central orchestration point. Wiring health check triggers into _run_pipeline() requires surgical changes. execute_all_waves() at line 3260 is currently called WITHOUT an on_wave_complete callback — adding one changes the calling pattern.
risks.mitigation: Keep integration points minimal — single runner.run_checks() calls at well-defined lifecycle events. All integration sites wrapped in try/except (TD-10). The on_wave_complete callback is already a defined parameter that defaults to None — passing it doesn't change execution behavior, it just activates unused code. No structural changes to _run_pipeline().

risks.description: Health checks run on lifecycle events from concurrent threads: RUNTIME_TICK from monitor thread, WAVE_COMPLETE from execution thread, ON_DEMAND from HTTP thread. Multiple checks trying to fail the same pipeline simultaneously could cause optimistic locking conflicts.
risks.mitigation: HealthCheckRunner uses per-pipeline locking (get_pipeline_state_lock) and optimistic versioning (expected_version). On VersionConflictError, reload pipeline and check if already FAILED (short-circuit). Per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances accessed only under pipeline lock (TD-11). Checks are pure functions — no locks held during check execution, especially during Tier 2 LLM calls.

risks.description: Tier 1 checks run on every lifecycle event including 10-second runtime ticks. Slow checks could delay the monitor loop.
risks.mitigation: Lazy context assembly — runtime tick checks only use in-memory state. Git operations only on PHASE_COMPLETE/WAVE_COMPLETE. 5s timeout per Tier 1 check. Performance test validates: 100 RUNTIME_TICK triggers < 1 second, no git operations.

risks.description: A health check incorrectly returning FAIL_PIPELINE would terminate a healthy pipeline, destroying in-progress work. Particularly risky for phase output presence (slow git push) and Tier 2 (LLM misinterpretation).
risks.mitigation: REVISION v2: Three-layer protection. (1) Two-strike confirmation (TD-7): first FAIL_PIPELINE is recorded but not enforced; only repeated FAIL_PIPELINE from the same check on the next trigger is applied. Checks with allow_immediate_fail=True (container liveness, startup reconciliation — where the container is verified absent from Docker) bypass this. (2) PhaseOutputPresenceCheck checks local branch head first (TD-7 note) — if local has commits but remote doesn't, returns DEGRADED, not FAILED. (3) HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=observe (TD-9) for initial rollout — events emitted but no pipeline state mutations.

risks.description: Tier 2 agent inspector depends on LLM API availability and response quality.
risks.mitigation: Inspector failures → DEGRADED/CONTINUE (non-blocking per TD-8). 30-second timeout. JSON mode for structured output. LLM prompt instructs to err on side of DEGRADED over FAILED. Two-strike confirmation means even a false FAILED from Tier 2 requires repetition before enforcement.

risks.description: Migrating startup reconciliation and container monitor to the new interface could change observable behavior (error messages, state mutation timing, event emission).
risks.mitigation: Preserve exact error messages. Behavioral equivalence tests compare original function output with migrated check output on same input. Keep original functions as deprecated wrappers.

risks.description: REVISION v2 addition. An unhandled exception in a health check could crash _run_pipeline(), the container monitor thread, or an HTTP handler, causing wider pipeline failures than the check was meant to prevent.
risks.mitigation: Two-layer exception isolation (TD-10). (1) Runner catches per-check exceptions and returns synthetic DEGRADED/CONTINUE. (2) Every integration site wraps run_checks() in try/except with logging. Startup and container monitor integration sites fall back to original functions on exception.

risks.description: REVISION v2 addition per RISK-8 from risk analyst. AgentCircuitBreaker in shared/egg_contracts/agent_recovery.py is NOT thread-safe — no locking on state transitions or counter mutations. If accessed from multiple threads, failure_count and state could be corrupted.
risks.mitigation: Per-pipeline instances stored in runner._circuit_breakers (TD-11). Each instance accessed only under per-pipeline lock during _apply_result(). No concurrent access to any single instance. Instances cleaned up on pipeline completion/failure.

risks.description: Tier 2 agent inspector makes LLM API calls at phase boundaries. With review cycles, costs could accumulate.
risks.mitigation: Haiku at ~$0.001/call. Typical pipeline: 3-4 PHASE_COMPLETE calls. Two-strike means most Tier 2 calls produce HEALTHY and don't trigger additional actions. Can disable Tier 2 via HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=disabled or by not setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

constraints: Tier 1 checks must be sub-second — no LLM calls, minimal git operations (use lazy context)
Tier 2 checks must not block phase transitions — 30-second timeout, treat failures as CONTINUE
Per-pipeline locking (get_pipeline_state_lock) and optimistic versioning (expected_version) required for all state mutations
Health check results capped at 10 per PhaseExecution to prevent state bloat
Backward compatibility: migrated startup reconciliation and container monitor must preserve existing error messages and state mutations
Network mode awareness: Tier 2 inspector works in both public and private modes (Anthropic API available in both via gateway proxy)
Each HealthCheck must be independently testable with mock PipelineHealthContext — no singleton access to Docker or state store inside check logic
HealthCheckRunner must be thread-safe — concurrent triggers from monitor, execution, and HTTP threads
No new EventType needed — use existing EventType.HEALTH_CHECK with structured data payload
Two-strike confirmation required for FAIL_PIPELINE actions (except allow_immediate_fail checks)
Exception isolation required at every integration site — health check failures must NEVER propagate to _run_pipeline(), container monitor, or HTTP handlers
HEALTH_CHECK_MODE environment variable must be respected at runtime — enforce/observe/disabled

open_questions_resolved.question: Should Tier 2 use the same model as agent sandboxes or a smaller model?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Use Haiku (TD-3). Structured evaluation task, not open-ended reasoning. Fast and cheap. Upgradeable per-check.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should FAIL_PIPELINE action be automatic or advisory?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Automatic with two-strike confirmation (TD-7, revised per REC-2). First FAIL_PIPELINE is recorded but downgraded to ALERT. Repeated FAIL_PIPELINE from same check on next trigger is enforced. Checks with allow_immediate_fail=True bypass two-strike. Runner also consults AgentRetryManager before failing — retries first if available.

open_questions_resolved.question: Where should health check results be persisted?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: PhaseExecution.health_checks, capped at 10 (TD-5). Keeps phase state in one place, avoids separate artifact lifecycle.

open_questions_resolved.question: What triggers Tier 2?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Always at PHASE_COMPLETE. At WAVE_COMPLETE only if Tier 1 returned DEGRADED. On-demand via REST endpoint (TD-6).

open_questions_resolved.question: Should health checks interact with AgentRetryManager?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Yes (TD-7). Runner consults retry/circuit-breaker logic before applying FAIL_PIPELINE. Per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances avoid thread-safety issues (TD-11).

open_questions_resolved.question: How to prevent false positive pipeline termination?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Three-layer protection (risk-4 mitigation): (1) Two-strike confirmation with allow_immediate_fail override (TD-7). (2) PhaseOutputPresenceCheck checks local branch head first. (3) HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=observe for initial rollout (TD-9).

open_questions_resolved.question: How to ensure health checks don't crash pipeline execution?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Two-layer exception isolation (TD-10): runner catches per-check exceptions, integration sites catch runner exceptions. Startup and container monitor fall back to original functions on exception.

open_questions_resolved.question: How to safely roll out the health check framework?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: HEALTH_CHECK_MODE environment variable (TD-9): start with 'observe' (emit events, no state mutations), graduate to 'enforce' once confidence is established. 'disabled' turns off entirely.

open_questions_resolved.question: Should the implementation be split into 2 PRs (Tier 1 first, Tier 2 second)?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Single PR (TD-12). HEALTH_CHECK_MODE=observe provides the same rollout safety as staged PRs. Interface designed for both tiers from the start. Tier 2 is only 2 files with well-isolated scope. If review capacity is a concern, the PR can be reviewed in two logical passes.

critical_1_fail_pipeline_two_strike.feedback: TASK-1-4 (runner) should include a 'two-strike' confirmation mechanism for FAIL_PIPELINE actions. PhaseOutputPresenceCheck (TASK-5-1) should check LOCAL branch head first.
changes: TD-7 revised: two-strike confirmation is now integral to HealthCheckRunner design. _pending_failures dict tracks (pipeline_id, check_name) -> first failure. Second FAIL_PIPELINE from same check on next trigger enforces.

HealthCheck base class gains allow_immediate_fail property (default False). StartupReconciliationCheck and ContainerLivenessCheck set allow_immediate_fail=True (container verified absent from Docker — false positive impossible).
PhaseOutputPresenceCheck (phase-6) now checks local branch head first via context.local_branch_head. If local has commits but remote doesn't, returns DEGRADED (push may be in progress), not FAILED.
PipelineHealthContext gains local_branch_head lazy property.

high_2_exception_isolation.feedback: Every call to run_checks() at integration sites must be wrapped in try/except. Runner should catch exceptions from individual checks.
changes: TD-10 added: two-layer exception isolation. Runner catches per-check exceptions. Integration sites catch runner exceptions.
TASK-1-4 (phase-2, runner): runner wraps each individual check in try/except, returns synthetic DEGRADED/CONTINUE on exception.

Phase 7 (phase-11, lifecycle wiring): every integration site (cli.py, container_monitor.py, multi_agent.py, pipelines.py) explicitly wraps run_checks() in try/except with logging. cli.py and container_monitor.py fall back to original functions on exception.
Acceptance criteria on all Phase 7 tasks now explicitly require: 'Health check exceptions are caught and logged at the integration site; they never propagate to the pipeline execution thread.'

medium_3_kill_switch.feedback: HEALTH_CHECK_MODE environment variable (enforce/observe/disabled) for safe production rollout.
changes: TD-9 added: HEALTH_CHECK_MODE with three modes. Default is 'enforce'. 'observe' emits events but never mutates pipeline state. 'disabled' skips all checks.
HealthCheckMode enum added to types.py (phase-1).
HealthCheckRunner reads HEALTH_CHECK_MODE in run_checks() (phase-2).
Integration tests verify all three modes (phase-13).

minor_documentation.feedback: Plan does not mention documentation updates for the new POST endpoint.
changes: Phase 11 (lifecycle wiring): health.py task includes 'Document the endpoint with docstring describing request/response format.'
TD-11 added: per-pipeline AgentCircuitBreaker instances accessed only under per-pipeline lock.
risk-8 added to risk table.
Codebase research confirmed: AgentCircuitBreaker has NO locking, IS NOT used in production. Orchestrator's own CircuitBreaker in resilience.py IS thread-safe but has different semantics.

minor_2pr_split.feedback: Plan should acknowledge the 2-PR split decision and justify it.
changes: TD-12 added with explicit justification for single-PR approach.
recommended_approach.single_pr_justification field added with detailed reasoning.
Acknowledges REC-1 is valid alternative if team prefers it.

minor_test_coverage.feedback: Phase 8 tests should include exception isolation tests and RUNTIME_TICK performance test.
changes: Phase 12 (unit tests): runner tests now include exception isolation test (check raising exception produces DEGRADED/CONTINUE), HEALTH_CHECK_MODE tests, two-strike confirmation tests.
Phase 13 (integration tests): explicit exception isolation tests for each integration site, performance test (100 RUNTIME_TICK < 1s), HEALTH_CHECK_MODE integration tests.
